title: Paired Square Roots
statement:
Let $\{a_i\}$ and $\{b_i\}$ be sequences of real numbers. Prove that
$$\sum_{m,n=1}^{2020}\dfrac{a_mb_n}{(\sqrt{m}+\sqrt{n})^2}\le 2\left(\sum_{m=1}^{2020}a_m^2\right)^{1/2}\left(\sum_{n=1}^{2020}b_n^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
hints: Split each term $\dfrac{a_mb_n}{(\sqrt{m}+\sqrt{n})^2}$ into a factor containing $a_m$ times a factor containing $b_n$, weighted so that after squaring, each inner sum over the other index is bounded by a constant.

Apply the Cauchy inequality to the factors $\dfrac{a_m}{\sqrt{m}+\sqrt{n}}\left(\dfrac{m}{n}\right)^{1/4}$ and $\dfrac{b_n}{\sqrt{m}+\sqrt{n}}\left(\dfrac{n}{m}\right)^{1/4}$. It then suffices to prove $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{2020}\dfrac{1}{(\sqrt{m}+\sqrt{n})^2}\left(\dfrac{m}{n}\right)^{1/2}\le 2$ for each $m$, and the same with $m$ and $n$ swapped.
Bound each term of that sum by $2\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\frac{n-1}{m}}+1}-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\frac{n}{m}}+1}\right)$, which telescopes.
solution: Proof. The left side of the inequality is $$\sum_{m,n=1}^{2020}\left[\dfrac{a_m}{\sqrt{m}+\sqrt{n}}\left(\dfrac{m}{n}\right)^{1/4}\right]\left[\dfrac{b_n}{\sqrt{m}+\sqrt{n}}\left(\dfrac{n}{m}\right)^{1/4}\right].$$ By the Cauchy inequality, $$\sum_{m,n=1}^{2020}\left[\dfrac{a_m}{\sqrt{m}+\sqrt{n}}\left(\dfrac{m}{n}\right)^{1/4}\right]\left[\dfrac{b_n}{\sqrt{m}+\sqrt{n}}\left(\dfrac{n}{m}\right)^{1/4}\right]\le\left(\sum_{m,n=1}^{2020}\left[\dfrac{a_m}{\sqrt{m}+\sqrt{n}}\left(\dfrac{m}{n}\right)^{1/4}\right]^2\right)^{1/2}\left(\sum_{m,n=1}^{2020}\left[\dfrac{b_n}{\sqrt{m}+\sqrt{n}}\left(\dfrac{n}{m}\right)^{1/4}\right]^2\right)^{1/2}.$$ From the identities $$\sum_{m,n=1}^{2020}\left[\dfrac{a_m}{\sqrt{m}+\sqrt{n}}\left(\dfrac{m}{n}\right)^{1/4}\right]^2=\sum_{m=1}^{2020}a_m^2\sum_{n=1}^{2020}\left[\dfrac{1}{(\sqrt{m}+\sqrt{n})^2}\left(\dfrac{m}{n}\right)^{1/2}\right]$$ and $$\sum_{m,n=1}^{2020}\left[\dfrac{b_n}{\sqrt{m}+\sqrt{n}}\left(\dfrac{n}{m}\right)^{1/4}\right]^2=\sum_{n=1}^{2020}b_n^2\sum_{m=1}^{2020}\left[\dfrac{1}{(\sqrt{m}+\sqrt{n})^2}\left(\dfrac{n}{m}\right)^{1/2}\right],$$ it suffices to prove $$\sum_{n=1}^{2020}\left[\dfrac{1}{(\sqrt{m}+\sqrt{n})^2}\left(\dfrac{m}{n}\right)^{1/2}\right]\le 2 \qquad (1)$$ and $$\sum_{m=1}^{2020}\left[\dfrac{1}{(\sqrt{m}+\sqrt{n})^2}\left(\dfrac{n}{m}\right)^{1/2}\right]\le 2. \qquad (2)$$ These two inequalities are the same ($m$ and $n$ swapped). We now prove $$\dfrac{1}{(\sqrt{m}+\sqrt{n})^2}\left(\dfrac{m}{n}\right)^{1/2}\le 2\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\dfrac{n-1}{m}}+1}-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\dfrac{n}{m}}+1}\right). \qquad (3)$$ This inequality is equivalent to $$\dfrac{1}{(\sqrt{m}+\sqrt{n})^2}\left(\dfrac{m}{n}\right)^{1/2}\le 2\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{m}}{\sqrt{n-1}+\sqrt{m}}-\dfrac{\sqrt{m}}{\sqrt{n}+\sqrt{m}}\right)\iff$$ $$\dfrac{1}{(\sqrt{m}+\sqrt{n})^2}\cdot\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\le 2\cdot\dfrac{\sqrt{n}-\sqrt{n-1}}{(\sqrt{n-1}+\sqrt{m})(\sqrt{n}+\sqrt{m})},$$ and from $(\sqrt{n-1}+\sqrt{m})(\sqrt{n}+\sqrt{m})\le(\sqrt{m}+\sqrt{n})^2$ and $2(\sqrt{n}-\sqrt{n-1})=\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{n}+\sqrt{n-1}}\ge\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{n}}$, the last inequality holds. Summing (3) gives (1), as required. $\blacksquare$

rubric.criterion: Applies the Cauchy inequality to the split $\left[\frac{a_m}{\sqrt{m}+\sqrt{n}}\left(\frac{m}{n}\right)^{1/4}\right]\left[\frac{b_n}{\sqrt{m}+\sqrt{n}}\left(\frac{n}{m}\right)^{1/4}\right]$, or an equivalent weighting, and reduces the problem to (1) and (2).
Proves inequality (3), or another bound on each term of (1) whose sum over $n$ is at most $2$.
Sums (3) to obtain (1), obtains (2) by swapping $m$ and $n$, and concludes.

fatal_errors.error: Applies the Cauchy inequality without weights such as $\left(\frac{m}{n}\right)^{1/4}$, so the remaining sums are not bounded by a constant.
Proves (1) but does not explain why (2) also holds or how the two give the result.
